import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the catplot (bar plot)
# Using catplot is great for this as it automatically calculates the mean (survival rate)
# and provides confidence intervals.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis',
    height=6,
    aspect=1.5,
    legend=False, # We will create a custom legend
    order=['First', 'Second', 'Third']
)

# Access the axes to customize further
ax = g.ax

# --- Customization and Annotations ---

# Set title and labels with more descriptive text
g.fig.suptitle('Survival Rate on the Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex', fontsize=20, y=1.03)
g.set_axis_labels('Passenger Class', 'Survival Rate', fontsize=14)
g.set_xticklabels(fontsize=12)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1) # Set y-axis limit to be from 0 to 100%

# Add annotations (text labels) on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    if height > 0: # Avoid annotating zero-height bars
        ax.annotate(f'{height:.1%}',
                    (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                    ha='center',
                    va='center',
                    fontsize=12,
                    color='black',
                    xytext=(0, 10),
                    textcoords='offset points')

# Improve the legend
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', labels=['Male', 'Female'], fontsize=12, title_fontsize=14)

# Adjust layout to make room for the title
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
